title: Scripture: free forgiveness; Christ's passion the sole merit
source_text: XXXVII. Id manifeste Scriptura Sacra docet, dum ait, Deum gratuito donare nobis omnes offensas, Coloss. 2. 13. Item quum toties repetit & inculcat nos servari & justificari gratia, per Dei gratiam, & non ex operibus, Rom. 3. Ephes. 2. Tit. 3. Nec enim cuiquam dubium esse potest, quin salus illa & justifi-catio remissionem peccatorum includat. Adeoque Christi passio & obedientia usque ad mortem crucis, unicum est illud meritum quo Deus movetur ad nobis largiendam delictorum veniam, nosque a peccati reatu liberandos. Unde est quod Apostolus ait, Nos in Christo habere redemptionem per sanguinem ejus, id est, remissionem peccatorum: nosque justificari per redemptionem quae est in Christo Jesu; quem proposuit Deus pro-pitiationem per fidem in sanguine ipsius.
pass_a_gloss: Holy Scripture teaches this plainly when it says that God freely gives us all offenses (Colossians 2:13). Likewise when it so often repeats and inculcates that we are saved and justified by grace, by God's grace, and not of works (Romans 3; Ephesians 2; Titus 3). For no one can doubt that that salvation and justification includes the remission of sins. And therefore Christ's passion and obedience unto the death of the cross is the sole merit by which God is moved to grant us pardon of faults and to free us from the guilt of sin. Hence the Apostle says that we have in Christ redemption through his blood, that is, the remission of sins; and that we are justified through the redemption that is in Christ Jesus, whom God set forth as a propitiation through faith in his blood.
pass_b_english: Scripture: God freely forgives all offenses; we are saved/justified by grace, not works.
Christ's passion and obedience unto death is the sole merit moving God to pardon.

choices.why: Key lemma for De Justitia densify §1071.
